agent_vs_you: The agent's plan is right: the exact supplied words to a voice, laid over the user's silent clip with assemble, no music, no captions, the clip's own length kept. (The write step is redundant, since voice could take the words directly, but harmless: narration.txt holds the exact script.) The words were lost inside our voice tool: it reads any line that starts 'Capitalised words: ...' as a 'Name: line' dialogue label, so 'Make mornings easier:' became a speaker name and was never spoken. Nothing in the catalogue warns about that, and the agent could not have known. Knowing it, I would keep the exact words but replace the colon after 'easier' with a dash in the voice input, which reads the same aloud.

your_plan.say: I'll record your exact words in a warm, clear English voice and lay them over your clip from the start, leaving the video as it is. No music, no captions.

steps.why: The exact supplied words, read once, about 8 s; the dash avoids the tool's 'Name:' speaker parsing and reads the same aloud.

fix: Harness (tools/voice.js): treat 'Label: text' as a speaker only when the plan marks the script as a dialogue (extra 'dialogue' or a write node made for two voices), or when at least two different labels each start a line and the label is a short name (one or two words, no verb); otherwise speak the whole line. Also have the voice step read its output back (transcribe and compare with the input words, as lettering is read back) and redo once on a missing word. Generalises: every script with a colon in its first sentence ('Pro tip: ...', 'Remember: ...') is clipped today.
